newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel slides against basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel slides against basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday as investors repaid yen-linked loans, dealers said.
"The basket rose sharply today as investors started repaying yen-linked loans following the recent rise of the yen against the dollar," said Guy Levi, a dealer at Bank Leumi.
Many Israeli companies turned to foreign currency loans during the last two years because of high domestic interest rates.
"The rise of the basket pushed the shekel downwards against the dollar despite the decline of the U.S. currency abroad on Monday," he added.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4010 shekels against 3.3990 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6961 shekels against 3.6877 on Friday.
The Bank of Israel had no representative rate on Monday because of the Independence Day holiday.
Late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4020 shekels.
Levi said that in the short run more companies could decide to repay foreign currency loans because of uncertainty regarding the direction of the dollar.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 2.8543 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7719 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9994 shekels compared with 1.9961 on Friday.
